# `silk/time/civil`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Calendar arithmetic of the ISO 8601 calendar on plain integers: leap years, month lengths, and
the conversion between a date and a day count.

## When to use

Most programs use `silk.time.plain_date`, which checks its values. Use these functions when a
parser or a formatter has the year, month, and day as numbers and a `PlainDate` is not needed.

## Details

The calendar is the proleptic Gregorian calendar: the leap year rule of today applies to every
year, also before 1582. Year 0 exists and is the year before year 1. Day counts are days since
`1970-01-01`, which is day 0.

## Gotchas

The functions do not check their arguments. A month outside 1 to 12 gives a result without
meaning.

## Examples

### Convert a date to a day count and back

```silk
import silk.time.civil as Civil

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let days = Civil.daysFromCivil(2000, 3, 1)
  if days != 11017 {
    return 1
  }
  let date = Civil.civilFromDays(days)
  if date.year != 2000 || date.month != 3 || date.day != 1 {
    return 2
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `civil` with `import silk.time.civil as civil`.

## `CivilDate`

```silk
pub struct CivilDate
```

A year, a month from 1 to 12, and a day of the month from 1, as plain numbers.

### Details

The fields are not checked, so a value can name a day that does not exist. `PlainDate` in
`silk.time.plain_date` is the checked type.

<a id="CivilDate.year"></a>

### Field `year`

```silk
pub year: i32
```

The year. Year 0 is the year before year 1.

<a id="CivilDate.month"></a>


<a id="CivilDate.day"></a>

### Field `day`

The day of the month, from 1.

<a id="isLeapYear"></a>

## `isLeapYear`

```silk
pub fn isLeapYear(year: i32) -> bool
```

Returns `true` if `year` has 366 days: it divides by 4, and not by 100 unless also by 400.

<a id="daysInYear"></a>

## `daysInYear`

```silk
pub fn daysInYear(year: i32) -> u16
```

Returns the number of days in `year`: 366 for a leap year, 365 otherwise.

<a id="daysInMonth"></a>

## `daysInMonth`

```silk
pub fn daysInMonth(year: i32, month: u8) -> u8
```

Returns the number of days in the month `month` of `year`, from 28 to 31.

### Gotchas

`month` must be from 1 to 12. Another value gives a result without meaning.

<a id="daysFromCivil"></a>

## `daysFromCivil`

```silk
pub fn daysFromCivil(year: i32, month: u8, day: u8) -> i64
```

Returns the number of days from `1970-01-01` to the given date. It is negative for an earlier
date.

### Gotchas

The date is not checked. `month` must be from 1 to 12; a `day` past the end of the month counts
on into the next month.

<a id="civilFromDays"></a>

## `civilFromDays`

```silk
pub fn civilFromDays(days: i64) -> CivilDate
```

Returns the date that is `days` days after `1970-01-01`. `days` can be negative.

### Gotchas

The year must fit an `i32`, so `days` must be within about 784 billion of zero. A count outside
that range traps.

<a id="weekdayFromDays"></a>

## `weekdayFromDays`

```silk
pub fn weekdayFromDays(days: i64) -> u8
```

Returns the ISO 8601 day of the week of the day `days` days after `1970-01-01`: 1 for Monday to
7 for Sunday.

<a id="dayOfYear"></a>

## `dayOfYear`

```silk
pub fn dayOfYear(year: i32, month: u8, day: u8) -> u16
```

Returns the day of the year of the given date: 1 for January 1, up to 366.

### Gotchas

The date is not checked. `month` must be from 1 to 12.
